decisive_items: lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
lytic destruction with cortical fracture of the T1 and T2 vertebrae
response.rationale: Large anterior mediastinal mass with bone destruction and hematologic concern in a young adult favors lymphoma; R5 is the broad lymphoma category, while R1 (NHL) is a plausible subtype but less specific without histology.

rejected.why: Thymoma typically anterior mediastinal but less likely with lytic bone lesions and hematologic concern.
Germ cell tumor can be mediastinal but lacks typical markers and bone destruction pattern.
Ewing sarcoma usually primary bone tumor; mediastinal mass with pleural involvement less typical.
Castleman disease can present with mediastinal mass but less aggressive with bone destruction and respiratory failure.
Hodgkin lymphoma possible but less common than NHL in this demographic; R5 covers both.
